To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
degradation models are a powerful approach in predicting the critical failure time of the electrical components and systems.

(i) the degradation models can be used to predict the critical point in time to perform maintenance for the distributed electrical networks; (ii) GP and AR models are the two most popular models in this area; (iii) GP and AR model are two different approaches in modeling the degradation process; (iv) the AR model requires more information to predict the future behavior of the degradation; (v) AR model is more accurate and more reliable than GP model; (vi) the accuracy and reliability
degradation-based models can be used to predict the future health of the system based on the current and past condition of the asset.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing the degradation models for the critical components of a distributed electrical system.
the development of the predictive models for PHM in the context of the distributed electrical networks.
the development of the first hitting time models for the distributed electrical networks to enhance the value of the critical assets by predicting the time of the first failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GP models are more suitable and applicable for the systems with the limited amount of available data, while the AR models are more suitable for the systems with a high amount of available data.
GP model is more suitable for the degradation models based on the available information and the complexity of the system.
the GP and AR models are the most reliable methods for the PHM of the distributed electrical power system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the degradation based models are the most valuable approach in order to obtain more reliable information especially for highly reliable assets, critical assets and recently developed products with high complexity.
the degradation models can be developed for any asset in the distributed electrical systems with the proper data acquisition, data analysis, and modeling.
the AR models have more advantages in terms of the computational cost and the ability to predict the critical times for initiating the maintenance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
these models are not only applicable to the electrical power systems but also to the other distributed systems such as transportation and manufacturing systems.
a combination of GP and AR models can provide more accurate and robust predictions of the critical failure time for the electrical systems.
the PHM can be a valuable tool in the electrical power systems to optimize the maintenance of the critical assets in order to enhance the value of the system.
